solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Upset concerning monarch's seat, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken word, so the spelling to write is a different one that sounds the same

blocks.note: over means about or concerning, as in a row over money
a monarch sits on a throne; the word said aloud matches a past participle of throw

explanation.surface: A rumour that the king's throne has been upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' sits at the front looking like an adjective about the seat, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A government that is overthrown has been toppled, which is the political sense of upset.

clue.text: Planting seeds without last of seeds due

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter alone
without means lacking, so a letter is taken out of the longer word

blocks.note: sowing is planting seeds
the final letter of seeds

explanation.surface: A gardener's job of planting seeds is overdue.
explanation.walkthrough: SOWING loses its S to leave OWING.
explanation.definitionFit: Money owing is money due, still to be paid: a plain synonym.

clue.text: Start on instruction, right away causing amusement

indicators.note: sending something away removes it, so this letter is dropped from the word before

blocks.note: to enter on something is to start it
training is instruction
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A command to begin a job immediately, which somebody finds funny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right away' reads as 'at once', but it splits into the abbreviation for right and the signal to remove it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something entertaining amuses its audience, so it is causing amusement: a synonym phrase.

clue.text: Go with one leaving Italian city

indicators.note: something leaving departs, so it is taken out of the longer word

blocks.note: Turin is a city in north-west Italy
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone travels with a companion who departs from an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' looks like a verb, but it is the noun: your go in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A go in a game is your turn, the noun sense of each word.

clue.text: Friends regularly hiding chap put in custody

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept
to hide something is to keep it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of Friends
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A group of friends shelter a man who is then taken into custody.
explanation.definitionFit: A court remands a defendant when it sends them back to custody to await trial.

clue.text: Wind with one in the opposite direction missing area

indicators.note: a thing missing is absent, so this letter is taken out

blocks.note: W is a standard abbreviation for with
a wind blowing from the east, the reverse direction
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A wind blowing the other way, with no area affected.
explanation.walkthrough: W, then EASTERLY minus its A. The clue cheekily defines the answer's opposite: 'one in the opposite direction' is the easterly wind.
explanation.definitionFit: A westerly is a wind blowing from the west, so it is a type of wind.

clue.text: Malagueña Ben dancing is too demanding

indicators.note: letters that are dancing move about and change places

blocks.note: taken as written, the tilde ignored
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man called Ben finds the Spanish malagueña dance too hard.
explanation.walkthrough: A malagueña is a flamenco-style dance from Málaga, so 'dancing' fits the surface perfectly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unmanageable cannot be handled because it asks too much, which is being too demanding.

clue.text: Sad case of whiskey leading to vomit

indicators.note: one part leading to another comes first, with the other following it

blocks.note: whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to retch is to try to vomit

explanation.surface: A sorry drunk whose whiskey makes them throw up.
explanation.definitionFit: A wretch is an unfortunate, pitiable person, which is what a sad case means as an idiom.

clue.text: Being physically fit, filled with energy in the meantime

definitions.note: interim is used as an adverb meaning meanwhile, though it is mostly an adjective or noun

indicators.note: something filled with a thing holds it inside

blocks.note: a fit person is in trim
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Keeping fit and energetic while waiting for something.
explanation.walkthrough: E goes inside IN TRIM after the T: IN T(E)RIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Interim arrangements hold for the time being, so interim corresponds to meanwhile.

clue.text: Older person dismissing one Spanish fellow

indicators.note: to dismiss someone is to send them out, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: a senior is an older person
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An elderly man sends away a younger Spanish companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Señor is the Spanish title for a man, like Mr, so it names a Spanish gentleman.

clue.text: Horrific travel by railway

indicators.note: one thing by another sits next to it, so the parts are placed side by side

blocks.note: to go is to travel
RY is an abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A frightening train journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Gory scenes are full of blood and violence, so they are horrific: a near-synonym.

clue.text: Be closely involved in short treatise about English

indicators.note: about means around, so one part goes round the other

blocks.note: taken as written
a tract is a short treatise or pamphlet
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Someone takes part in a brief essay about English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' tempts you to cut a letter off, but a tract is itself a short treatise.
explanation.definitionFit: To interact is to act on one another, so people who interact are closely involved.

clue.text: English National Opera dates raised in interval

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word means reading it from the bottom up

blocks.note: ENO is the English National Opera, a London company
dates are times

explanation.surface: An opera company's performance dates go up during the interval.
explanation.walkthrough: ENO TIMES read upwards gives SEMITONE. The surface makes 'interval' the break in an opera, but here it is the musical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a semitone is the smallest interval, the step between adjacent piano keys.

clue.text: Nation, say

blocks.note: first meaning: a country with its own government
second meaning: to declare or express in words

explanation.walkthrough: The comma makes 'say' look like 'for example', but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A state is a sovereign country, and to state something is to say it formally.

clue.text: Showing confidence about city firm

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first part goes round the second

blocks.note: someone sure is confident
EC is the postcode for the City of London, the financial district

explanation.surface: Someone is confident about a firm in the City.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Showing confidence' looks like the definition, but 'firm' is.
explanation.definitionFit: Something firm is fixed and stable, which is secure in the sense of fastened.

clue.text: Unwilling promise by left

indicators.note: one thing by another stands next to it, so the two parts are joined side by side

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
an oath is a solemn promise

explanation.surface: A reluctant vow made by someone who has departed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' is read as the direction, not the past tense of leave.
explanation.definitionFit: To be loath to do something is to be reluctant, so it is a synonym for unwilling.

clue.text: Right place set out for package

indicators.note: things set out are laid out afresh in a new arrangement

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for right
taken as written

explanation.surface: The proper spot is arranged for a delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: A parcel is a wrapped package sent by post: a direct synonym.

clue.text: Caliban upset about new man-eater?

indicators.note: a name that is upset is knocked over and its letters rearranged
about means around, so the rearranged letters go round the extra one

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's monster Caliban, from The Tempest, troubled about a man-eater.
explanation.walkthrough: Caliban's name is thought to be Shakespeare's near-anagram of cannibal, which is the joke behind the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A cannibal eats human flesh, so a man-eater is a literal description.

clue.text: Runs engine very swiftly when starting?

definitions.text: Runs engine very swiftly when starting?

indicators.note: the start of each word is its opening letter, so only those are kept

blocks.note: the opening letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A driver gunning the engine as the car sets off.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition, with the question mark flagging it.
explanation.definitionFit: A driver revs an engine by making it turn faster, which is often done when starting off.

clue.text: Brace of small fish, not old

indicators.note: not means without, so this letter is left out

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a trout is a freshwater fish
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A pair of small fish that are fresh, not old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brace' suggests a pair, as of game birds; here it is the structural support.
explanation.definitionFit: A strut is a bar that braces a structure, so brace as a noun means a strut.

clue.text: Quick profit involving cocaine

indicators.note: something involving another includes it, so one part sits inside

blocks.note: to pay is to be profitable, as in crime doesn't pay
C is slang for cocaine

explanation.surface: Fast money made from dealing drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Pacy means having pace, so fast or quick, a word used of sportspeople.

clue.text: Musical form with runs about note

blocks.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
on means about, as in a talk on art
do (doh) is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A piece of music with passages running around one note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like a signal to put one piece round another, but here it is a word in its own right.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondo is a musical form in which a main theme keeps returning between contrasting episodes.

clue.text: Room in church with a yellow light

blocks.note: CH is the abbreviation for church
amber is the yellow light on traffic lights

explanation.surface: A room in a church lit with a warm yellow glow.
explanation.definitionFit: A chamber is a room, especially a private or official one, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: End Ptolemy's shifting movement of eg troops

indicators.note: letters that are shifting move about into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The ending of the Ptolemaic dynasty as armies move about.
explanation.walkthrough: Ptolemy was the name of the Greek kings of ancient Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: Deployment is the positioning of forces ready for action, which is a movement of troops.
